headline: Single-sample long-read and single-cell methods sharpen regulatory variant and enhancer-gene inference
label: Cell Type Resolved Regulatory Profiling
summary: New preprints link regulatory inference to single samples or cells: FiberTron predicts variant effects from one Fiber-seq sample, and CREMAP refines peak-gene links.
synthesis: The dominant thread is extracting regulatory information at finer resolution from a single sample or single cells. FiberTron, a 12M-parameter model trained on one Fiber-seq/Nanopore sample, predicts base-resolution methylation and accessibility for regulatory variant effects. CREMAP removes shared latent technical and biological variation before testing peak-gene links in single-cell multi-omics, aiming to improve enhancer-gene mapping. Pooch uses differentially methylated CpGs to assign parent of origin across Hi-C-phased diploid genomes. The remaining items concern long-read genomics and quality control: LongPhase-S somatic haplotyping, donor-specific assemblies for somatic SVs, Kinnex RNA-seq for Mendelian diagnosis, sample mispairing benchmarks, and Phirefly phasing. They address adjacent questions rather than cell-type attribution of regulatory state.
